security_audit.summary: The skill contains legitimate frontend setup and bundling scripts, but those scripts execute package-manager commands and modify generated project files. Most Markdown and schema URL findings are false positives; the bundled shadcn-components.tar.gz archive remains a manual-review concern because static analysis could not inspect it.

remediation.issue: Shell scripts install dependencies and modify project files.
remediation.suggestion: Document the commands run by each script and require users to run them only in a new or disposable project directory.

remediation.issue: The setup script includes a bundled tarball that static analysis could not inspect.
remediation.suggestion: Publish an expanded file listing or replace the archive with plain source files so reviewers can audit every included component.

remediation.issue: The bundling script removes dist and bundle.html in the current project.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before bundling that existing build outputs with those names will be replaced.

content.value_statement: Complex artifacts often need reusable UI components and a modern frontend workflow. This skill creates a React and Tailwind project, then bundles it into one shareable HTML artifact.
actual_capabilities: Initializes a React 18 and TypeScript project with Vite.
Configures Tailwind CSS 3.4.1 with shadcn/ui theme variables.
Adds path aliases for imports under the generated src directory.
Installs Radix UI and shadcn/ui related dependencies.
Extracts bundled shadcn/ui components into the generated project.
Bundles the finished app into a single self-contained HTML file.
limitations: It is not intended for simple single-file HTML or JSX artifacts.
It requires Node.js 18 or newer and a working package manager environment.
It installs npm packages and can take time on slow networks.
The included component archive needs manual trust review before automated use.

use_cases.title: Prepare complex Claude artifacts
use_cases.description: Set up a modern artifact project when a response needs routing, component composition, or rich client-side behavior.

The project is built with Parcel and inlined into bundle.html as a single self-contained file.

output_examples.input: Add polished UI components to my artifact.
output_examples.output: The artifact uses cards, dialogs, tabs, forms, and other shadcn/ui components with consistent Tailwind styling.

best_practices: Run the initialization script in a new project directory to avoid overwriting existing work.
Use this skill for complex interactive artifacts, not for simple static HTML snippets.
Review generated dependencies and bundled output before sharing the final artifact.
anti_patterns: Do not run the scripts in a repository with unrelated uncommitted work.
Do not use the bundled output as a substitute for reviewing third-party dependencies.
Do not skip local testing when the artifact includes forms, navigation, or stateful behavior.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui project for building complex Claude HTML artifacts.

faq.question: Does it work for simple artifacts?
faq.answer: It can, but it is usually too heavy for simple single-file HTML or JSX artifacts.

faq.question: What tools does it require?
faq.answer: It requires Bash, Node.js 18 or newer, npm, pnpm, and access to install JavaScript packages.

faq.question: What file does the bundling script produce?
faq.answer: It produces bundle.html, a self-contained HTML file with JavaScript, CSS, and dependencies inlined.

faq.question: Does it make network requests?
faq.answer: The scripts install npm packages through the package manager. A shadcn/ui URL is also written as schema metadata.

faq.question: Is it safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: It should require user confirmation because it runs shell scripts, installs packages, writes files, and includes an unscanned component archive.
